handbookNote: Idaho Real Estate Broker license exam (Idaho's own naming: Associate Broker / Designated Broker tiers, both above Salesperson). Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Idaho Real Estate Commission (IREC), a bureau under DOPL. Exam mechanics confirmed via Pearson VUE's own official Candidate Handbook #091300 and Content Outline #091306. National/general portion: 80 scored items (+5 pretest), 150 minutes. Idaho state portion (Broker): 50 scored items (+5-10 pretest), 90 minutes. Total 130 scored items, 240 minutes (4 hours). Passing score is a proprietary SCALED score: 75 (0-100 scale) for Broker (Salesperson uses 70) -- explicitly not literal percent-correct, on EACH section independently; a candidate who fails only one section may retake just that section within 1 year of passing the other. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=130, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=98 (round(130*0.75)), same convention as UT/NV/KS Broker. NATIONAL PORTION (80 items) reuses the exact same real Pearson VUE national item bank as Utah/Nevada/Kansas -- Idaho's real Broker outline weights are IDENTICAL (10/8/10/15/12/9/8/8 across the same 8 sections) -- files copied directly rather than redrafted, a real, confirmed cross-state efficiency. IDAHO STATE PORTION (50 items, real % weights, Broker): Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission (4%, incl. the real Recovery Fund cap of $10,000 per licensee per calendar year, Idaho Code Section 54-2071), Licensing Requirements (4%, incl. the real 3-tier license structure -- Salesperson/Associate Broker/Designated Broker under Section 54-2011, Designated Broker's extra BCOO course + trust-account company registration), License Law and Rules of IREC (30%, largest section -- disciplinary grounds, trust account rules under Sections 54-2041-2046, advertising, recordkeeping, Recovery Fund mechanics), Brokerage Representation/Agency Law (20%, Idaho's real Brokerage Representation Act, Sections 54-2082-2096 -- Idaho notably has NO DEFAULT agency relationship absent a written agreement, unlike Kansas's transaction-broker default: an unrepresented party is simply a customer under Section 54-2086 until a written agreement is signed; the Act also statutorily abolishes common-law vicarious liability and fiduciary duty in favor of its own statutory duty scheme), Calculations and Closing Costs (10%, incl. Idaho-specific facts like the absence of a real estate transfer tax and arrears property-tax billing), Idaho Principles and Practices (12%, incl. Idaho's real community property law and prior-appropriation water-rights doctrine), and Brokerage Management (20%, real BROKER-ONLY content -- designated broker supervision under Section 54-2038, the $300 broker personal-funds trust account cap under Sections 54-2041-2047, branch office/recordkeeping rules). Governing law: Idaho Code Title 54, Chapter 20. This bank was drafted across 7 new state-topic drafting passes (the 8 national files were reused, not redrafted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
